title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: why not to all need not trouble the believer who holds just condemnation in Adam; Epist. 107 — Grace of God is not given to all men
pass_a_gloss: But why it is not given unto all ought not to move the believer, who believes that from one all went into most just condemnation. Lest I be too lengthy in heaping up testimonies, I will add that one alone which stands in Epistle 107, in which, among those twelve sentences which he affirms to pertain unto the Catholic faith, this second is, That the grace of God is not given unto all men.
pass_b_english: Why it is not given to all need not trouble the believer who holds that from one all went into most just condemnation. Not to pile witnesses: I add only Epistle 107, where among twelve sentences he affirms belong to catholic faith, the second is: The grace of God is not given to all men.
source_text: Cur autem non omnibus detur, fidelem movere non debet, qui credit ex uno omnes isse in condemnationem justissimam. Ne nimis multus sim in accumulandis testimoniis, illud unicum adjungam quod exstat Epistola cvii. in qua, inter duodecim illas sententias quae ad fidem Catholicam pertinere affirmat, haec secunda est, Gratiam Dei non dari omnibus hominibus.
